biography.plain_text: Andrei Ilyich Komarov is a Russian billionaire investor who built his fortune by acquiring and modernising Chelyabinsk Pipe Rolling Plant, or ChelPipe. His earlier career moved from theatre administration into metals trading and industrial ownership.

long_biography.plain_text:
The 'white metallurgy' model became Andrei Komarov's signature at ChelPipe: cleaner, highly automated plants designed to change both production and workplace culture. He paired large-scale modernisation with strict safety standards, digital systems and carefully organised industrial spaces, presenting heavy manufacturing as skilled, precise work.

That approach extended into workforce training. New equipment required operators able to use expensive, specialised machinery, so the group developed a vocational programme with regional education partners and built practical training around production needs. Komarov's industrial outlook had an unlikely prelude: before entering metals trading, the engineering graduate worked as an administrator at Moscow's Satiricon theatre.
